div.div: A gate is tested from both sides: the real baseline must PASS (the gate is not too tight) and every negative control must FAIL (the gate is not too loose)

THE REAL BASELINE
scheduling topic: accepted at binding 0.49 [I5] on the visible set, clearly below the cap 0.9 [I6]

LEGITIMATE-NOISE REFERENCES
legitimate runs (e.g. reduced precision, another device) that set each limit, per input set (B1)

IF ONE IS REJECTED: the gate is too tight.
In the first campaign the first gate rejected the real baseline; found the day the evaluator was built, because the baseline ran before any candidate.

THE FROZEN GATE (B2)
is finished only when, on EVERY input set, held-out included:
1. the baseline is ACCEPTED with margin clearly below 1
2. every control is REJECTED
re-run both on every evaluator version

FIRST CAMPAIGN (diffusion-model policy)
- fewer denoising steps -> correctness gate vs reference
- output scaled by 3 % [I1] -> calibrated per-dimension limits
- cached output -> inputs change per call; 'model ran once'
- perturbation on a second compute core -> correctness gate

SCHEDULING TOPIC
- starve_soft: never runs soft chains -> completion check (logging, telemetry never finish)
- not_ready: returns a job already started -> integrity check
- wallclock: unseeded random tie-break -> order probe (REJECTED at 53.5 ms [I2])

A CONTROL CAN BE WRONG TOO
The wallclock control first salted its tie-break with the parity of a nanosecond clock. On the development machine that clock had microsecond resolution, so the parity was always even: the control was accidentally deterministic and the order probe could not see it. Fix: an unseeded random generator. Rule: run each control and confirm it fails for the reason it was built for.

DEVELOPMENT HOST vs EVALUATION HOST
- development host: visible set only; its records are INVALID by design (scheduling topic quick mode: 4 seeds [I4]), so a development number is never taken for an official one
- evaluation host: visible + held-out sets, official runs only
- a device lock on each host keeps other work off the device during a timed run

WHY: a claim is scientific only if some observation could refute it (Popper 1959 [P3]). A gate that has never rejected a plausible cheat makes no claim; the rejected controls are the observations that show it can refute. Most fake results are accidents (a bug that skips work looks like a cheat); controls catch both.

Legend: green = legitimate runs that must pass | red = controls that must fail, and the too-tight failure | amber = the frozen gate | blue = hosts | purple = the principle | arrow label = required verdict

Sources. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown. [Pn] = public (cited paper, or my arithmetic on public mathematics); [In] = illustrative (a design parameter of the harness, a round value that keeps the shape of the first campaign, or output of the demonstration scheduling simulator; never a measurement of a real platform); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/B3-negative-controls.md (both control tables, 'a control can be wrong too', development vs evaluation host, device lock, Popper); notes/B2-the-frozen-evaluator.md; notes/B1-reference-and-baseline.md (legitimate-noise references); notes/C3-calibration.md (baseline binding, wallclock control rejected); notes/C4-lessons-about-the-method.md (gates fail both ways). The second-core perturbation's purpose is the notes' reading; the source names the control only.
[I1] c1_control_scale_illustrative = 3 %. illustrative; keeps the shape of the first campaign (internal methodology notes, 2026), not its values
[I2] sched_control_wallclock_ms = 53.5 ms. illustrative: demonstration run of the local scheduling simulator
[P3] pub_popper_year = 1959 year. public: Popper, The Logic of Scientific Discovery, English edition, Hutchinson, 1959
[I4] topic_quick_seeds = 4 seeds. illustrative: design parameter of the harness
[I5] sched_baseline = {median 34.7, min 32.3, max 45.4, binding_visible 0.49, binding_a 0.34, binding_b 0.44} ms / binding. illustrative: demonstration run of the local scheduling simulator
[I6] harness_margin_cap_scheduling = 0.9 binding ratio. illustrative: design parameter of the harness
